{{Quote|You cannot pass. Go back to the north seas and freeze.''"<br />"''Why, Master Protas?''"<br />"''Because it pleases me.|Protas and the aiwha pod, "The Tale of the Aiwha Pod"|<ref name="Tale" />}}
An '''aiwha pod''' from the [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] of [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] was, according to local [[The Tale of the Aiwha Pod|legend]], stopped by the [[Deity/Legends|god-beast]] [[Protas]] from swimming south for the [[Temperature/Legends|cold]] [[Winter/Legends|winter]]. Protas refused to let the [[Aiwha/Legends|aiwha]] continue on their migration and directed them back north to [[Death/Legends|perish]], forcing them into [[Destruction of Protas|battle]]. While they drew [[Blood/Legends|blood]], Protas endured their attacks until he eventually exposed his soft and vulnerable neck, allowing [[Unidentified aiwha|one]] of the aiwha to take advantage of the weakness. Protas thrashed his fins and killed the aiwha, but the latter's sacrifice allowed the rest of the [[Pod (social group)|pod]] to rally and deal a final, fatal blow to Protas.

==Description==
{{Quote|And that is why, to this day, the aiwha rule the oceans and are accorded a measure of respect even among the largest, most powerful, and most plentiful beasts.|Ryan Kaufman, "The Tale of the Aiwha Pod"|<ref name="Tale" />}}
[[File:Aiwha-wosfg.jpg|thumb|left|270px|The pod was made up of aiwha (pictured).]]
According to a legend of the [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoan]] [[Species/Legends|species]], "[[The Tale of the Aiwha Pod]]"&mdash;translated from [[Kaminoan (language)/Legends|Kaminoan]] by [[Ryan Kaufman]] into [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic]]&mdash;an [[Aiwha/Legends|aiwha]] [[Pod (social group)|pod]] lived in the [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] of<ref name="Tale" /> the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="Kamino">{{Film|II}}</ref> [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]]. During the [[Temperature/Legends|cold]] [[Winter/Legends|winter]], the aiwha of the pod would swim south to warmer [[Water/Legends|waters]]. The pod was ferocious and numerous, able to fight with unity and determination against any threat. Respectful to others, it did not seek glory in battle, and as such, it accorded great respect from all beasts of the oceans no matter the size, strength, or how numerous those beasts were.<ref name="Tale" />

==History==
{{Quote|The aiwha knew they could not return, that they would surely die in the north seas. We must fight, they told themselves. And so they did.|Ryan Kaufman, "The Tale of the Aiwha Pod"|<ref name="Tale" />}}
In the legend, the pod was traveling south for the increasingly cold winter. The [[Deity/Legends|god-beast]] [[Protas]], who had grown arrogant in his old age after [[Battle of Thalina|defeating]] the dark titan [[Melkorr]] and the sentient legion [[kikla]], came across the pod on their journey. He refused to let them pass and directed them to return north, where they would surely [[Death/Legends|perish]]. The pod queried Protas, asking for what reason did the god-beast have for desiring their death. Protas proclaimed it would please him, giving the pod no choice but death. Without warning, the pod decided as one to [[Destruction of Protas|attack]] Protas. Like Melkorr, they violently tore at his flesh, drawing [[Blood/Legends|blood]] but unable to inflict a wound of consequence. Likewise, they swarmed the god-beast much like the kikla swimmers, swarming Protas with a unity and determination the kikla did not possess. Still, Protas endured the pod's attacks.<ref name="Tale" />

Eventually, Protas exposed his soft and vulnerable neck, providing a gap in his defenses. One [[Unidentified aiwha|lone aiwha]] saw that, and with no regard to his own safety, attacked and bit down on the flesh. Protas gave a great bellow of pain and thrashed his fins, attempting to beat off the lone aiwha. While the self-sacrificing aiwha was broken by the blows, he did not release the neck of Protas, allowing the pod to rally and deal a final, fatal blow. Both the lone aiwha and Protas died, staining the waters with their blood. With their defeat, the aiwha came to rule the oceans of Kamino and were accorded great respect due to their victory without seeking glory.<ref name="Tale" />

==Behind the scenes==
The aiwha pod appeared in [[Ryan Kaufman (real person)|Ryan Kaufman's]] short story "[[The Tale of the Aiwha Pod (short story)|The Tale of the Aiwha Pod]]," published by [[Prima Games]] in [[2005]] within the ''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando: Prima Official Game Guide]]''.<ref name="Tale" />
